newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sleaze trial set for French Socialist leader.
newsitem.headline: Sleaze trial set for French Socialist leader.

text.p: The newly-elected leader of Socialist deputies in the French National Assembly will stand trial in Nantes, western France, on charges of favouritism in the award of a public works contract, justice sources said on Thursday.
They said the charge against Jean-Marc Ayrault, who is also deputy mayor of Nantes, arose from a 1995 inquiry into the office of information and communication, a part of the Nantes city hall.
At issue was the award, on a non-competitive basis, of an advertising contract for a city magazine to a Nantes advertising agency.
No date was given for the trial. If convicted, Ayrault could be jailed for up to two years and fined as much as 200,000 francs ($34,000).
